system.summary: Telegrams sent without encipherment, directly in the Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit groups), 1913-1914 and June 1916. Telegrams from the same file sent without encipherment, directly in Chinese telegraph code: Li Yuanhong’s reply to Huang Xing (14 June), Huang Xing’s message to Tan Renfeng about Li Yuanhong, a telegram of Huang Xing about Shaanxi, one to Mukden, and a short message signed 亞; then, in the next volume (June–November 1916), the Shanghai notables’ appeal to Huang Xing (25 June), his salute to the rallied fleet (27 June), messages signed 羣 and 鍾 (July–August) and the telegrams sent to Shanghai after his death (November).

prior_solution.where: Not in this repository (pointer only in sunyatsen/y1916); no decipherment on the JACAR copies; Cryptiana checked.

texts.summary: Telegrams sent without encipherment, directly in the Chinese standard telegraph code (four-digit groups), 1913-1914 and June 1916. Telegrams from the same file sent without encipherment, directly in Chinese telegraph code: Li Yuanhong’s reply to Huang Xing (14 June), Huang Xing’s message to Tan Renfeng about Li Yuanhong, a telegram of Huang Xing about Shaanxi, one to Mukden, and a short message signed 亞; then, in the next volume (June–November 1916), the Shanghai notables’ appeal to Huang Xing (25 June), his salute to the rallied fleet (27 June), messages signed 羣 and 鍾 (July–August) and the telegrams sent to Shanghai after his death (November).

reading_review.note: 20 plain-code telegrams, all coherent wenyan telegram style, incl. Li Yuanhong's long reply to Huang Xing (N34) and the Shanghai notables' appeal (V4A); doubtful codes are mostly marked emendations of digit slips, densest in V4C (19 of 70, restored stock phrase 挽旣倒之狂瀾，作中流之砥柱).
